deep.reconstruction:
Context: Fredholm theory for nuclear (trace-class) operators on Hilbert space. This is the material that became Grothendieck's 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 84, 1956). On the previous page R(u) = Σ P_n(u) = det(1+u)(1+u)^{-1} is the Fredholm 'first minor' (the adjugate of 1+u). This gives (1+u)^{-1} = 1 - u R(u)/det(1+u). For hermitian nuclear u = Σ λ_i e_i⊗e_i', R(u) is diagonal in the same basis with eigenvalues ρ_i = ∏_{j≠i}(1+λ_j) = det(1+u)/(1+λ_i). From this he proved |R(u)| ≤ R(|u|) and, for u ≥ 0, 0 ≤ R(u) ≤ det(1+u)·1. The corollary (***) is ||R(u)||_∞ ≤ ||R(|u|)||_∞ ≤ det(1+|u|) ≤ e^{||u||_1}.

This page examines how sharp (***) is. Because u is nuclear in infinite dimension, the eigenvalues λ_i tend to 0. Hence ρ_i → det(1+u), and so ||R(u)|| ≥ |det(1+u)|. For u ≥ 0 this lower bound combines with 0 ≤ R(u) ≤ det(1+u) to give equality: ||R(u)|| = det(1+u). Grothendieck therefore remarks that inequality (***) a) is 'presque inattendue' (almost unexpected), since it is an equality for u ≥ 0. The bound det(1+|u|) is thus optimal on the positive cone.

The rest of the page holds faint erased drafts of the same estimates, e.g. ||R(u)|| ≤ det(1+|u|) and products ∏(1+λ_i).
errors: 'det(1+λu)' in the definition of ρ_i should read det(1+u).
The lower bound uses infinite dimension, or a zero eigenvalue, so that some λ_i is arbitrarily small. In finite dimension with all λ_i ≠ 0, ||R(u)|| ≥ |det(1+u)| can fail.

The argument is given only for hermitian u. It does extend to any nuclear u in infinite dimension: (1+u)^{-1} is a compact perturbation of 1, so its spectrum contains 1 and its norm is at least 1. That extension is not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Eigenvalues of the Fredholm adjugate R(u)=det(1+u)(1+u)^{-1} for hermitian trace-class u are ∏_{j≠i}(1+λ_j); hence ||R(u)|| ≥ |det(1+u)|, with equality for u ≥ 0
ideas.modern_name: Sharpness of the Carleman-type bound ||det(1+A)(1+A)^{-1}|| ≤ det(1+|A|) ≤ exp||A||_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Carleman (Hilbert–Schmidt case); trace-class version in Grothendieck 1956 and in Gohberg–Krein and Simon (Trace Ideals)
ideas.where_published: Closest is 'La théorie de Fredholm', Bull. SMF 84 (1956); whether the sharpness remark itself appears there is unsure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine sharpness check of a standard Fredholm-determinant estimate. The material is essentially absorbed into Grothendieck's 1956 Fredholm paper and the standard trace-ideal literature.
transcription_corrections: 'ρ_i = det(1+λu)/(1+λ_i)' should be read as ρ_i = det(1+u)/(1+λ_i).
The last line reads 'elle devient égalité pour u ≥ 0 !'
